Context/Background:
Tumor-infiltrating B cells play a significant role in tumor development, progression, and prognosis, yet a comprehensive classification system is lacking. To address this gap, we present a pan-cancer single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas of tumor-infiltrating B and plasma cells across a large sample cohort. 

We isolated B cells and plasma cells from 15 studies spanning 7 cancer types as data sources. After applying batch correction and integrating the data, we removed low-quality cells and determined the optimal number of clusters. Using standard Seurat methods for integration, clustering, and differential expression analysis, we confirmed the absence of batch effects, with no study- or cancer type-specific clusters. 

We employed a graph-based clustering method to identify TIL-Bs with recurring phenotypes, uncovering a total of 10 clusters. Step one of cluster annotation used canonical markers like CD19 and MS4A1 (CD20), which are prevalent throughout B cell development but decline in plasma cells. Markers such as CD38, JCHAIN, and SDC1 (CD138) are prominent in plasma cells, but less so in earlier stages. This revealed four B cell clusters, two intermediate clusters with proliferative and germinal center (GC) features, and four plasma cell clusters.
Prompt: Based on upregulated pathways and differentially expressed markers in each cluster, assign functional phenotypes to each of the 4 B-cell clusters (clusters 1-4).  Provide a discussion of the reasoning behind cluster assignments, highlighting important genes and pathways where relevant.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The authors generated a pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas of tumor-infiltrating B cells from seven cancer types (15 studies), integrated via Seurat, and identified four clusters of mature B cells (clusters 1–4). Differential markers and pathway enrichments for each cluster are provided in four CSVs (cluster 1–4 DE tables). No study- or tumor-type–specific biases were noted (“batch effects absent,” “clusters not cancer-type specific”).  

Keywords  
• Germinal center (GC)  
• Naive B cell  
• NF-κB/TNF signaling  
• Interferon response  
• Antigen presentation  

Candidate Genes  
• MYC (and Myc targets)  
• CD69, CCR7, CD83  
• DUSP4, CD86, HLA-DPB1  
• LY86, BLK, LTB  

1) Cluster 1 – GC Dark-Zone–Like B Cells  
Key markers/DE: SNX9, TMEM230, RER1, GPR183 (EBI2), CXCR4, TCL1A, FCER2, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DPB1  
ORA highlights Myc Targets (MSigDB_Hallmark V1; 9/200 genes, adj p ≈1.4×10⁻⁷) and hematopoietic lineages (e.g. FCER2, IL4R, HLA-DP alleles). MYC-driven transcription is a hallmark of dark-zone GC B cells undergoing proliferation. High CXCR4 and EBI2 (GPR183) direct dark-zone homing.  
Phenotype → “Proliferative GC dark-zone B cells”  

2) Cluster 2 – Resting/Naive B Cells  
Key markers/DE: LY86, BLK, LTB, MARCHF1 (all with small avg_log2FC). Only four genes passed DE thresholds, with no significant ORA (insufficient gene count). LY86 and BLK are characteristic of naive, pre-GC B cells; LTB supports lymphoid architecture.  
Phenotype → “Resting naive/transitional B cells”  

3) Cluster 3 – Interferon-Activated Antigen-Presenting B Cells  
Key markers/DE: DUSP4, CD82, CD86, ISG15, IFI44L, IFITM1, HLA-DPB1, SPIB, GBP4, MS4A1  
ORA enriched for Interferon Alpha/Gamma Response (MSigDB_Hallmark, adj p < 5×10⁻⁷), B cell receptor signaling, regulation of actin cytoskeleton, phagocytosis and pathogenic bacterial‐infection pathways. Upregulation of CD86, HLA-DP alleles, and ISGs suggests potent antigen presentation under interferon stimulation.  
Phenotype → “IFN-activated, antigen-presenting effector B cells”  

4) Cluster 4 – GC Light-Zone–Like/Activated Memory B Cells  
Key markers/DE: CD69, CCR7, SLC2A3, REL, NR4A2, CD83, NFKBID, BCL2A1, CXCR5, HLA-DRA, JUNB, IRF8  
ORA shows TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB (MSigDB_Hallmark, adj p ≈1.1×10⁻⁹), antigen processing/presentation, and allograft-rejection/autoinflammation pathways. CD83 and CD69 mark activated GC light-zone B cells; CCR7/CXCR5 guide LZ positioning. NF-κB targets (REL, NFKBID, BCL2A1) support survival and selection in the light zone.  
Phenotype → “Activated GC light-zone/memory‐precursor B cells”  

Discussion  
Clusters 1 and 4 both map to GC biology but to different microanatomical zones: cluster 1 shows MYC targets and dark-zone homing receptors (CXCR4, EBI2), consistent with proliferative GC dark-zone B cells; cluster 4 exhibits NF-κB–driven activation, antigen-presentation, and light-zone homing cues (CCR7, CD83). Cluster 2’s minimal DE changes and expression of naive-markers (LY86, BLK) define a resting state. Cluster 3 bridges adaptive and innate immunity with strong interferon signatures (ISGs, HLA upregulation) and cytoskeletal remodeling, indicating an antigen-presenting effector B cell ready for T-cell interaction.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate the dark-zone vs. light-zone mapping by checking expression of DZ/LZ signature genes (e.g., AICDA, CD86) via targeted assays.  
2. Assess somatic hypermutation rates per cluster to confirm GC status.  
3. Functionally test antigen presentation capability of cluster 3 B cells in vitro (e.g., T-cell activation assays).  
4. Examine co-expression of plasma-cell markers (CD38, SDC1) to ensure clusters 1–4 do not include early plasmablast stages.
